clue.text: River Test commercial

parts.note: the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An angler's note about fishing rights on the River Test being sold off for commercial use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Test' reads as the Hampshire chalk stream famous for trout fishing, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as adjectives: industrial and commercial both describe trade and business activity.

clue.text: Yours truly is a leader in mosque!

definitions.text: Yours truly is a leader in mosque!

parts.note: the setter calling themself 'yours truly', with 'is', gives I'M

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word mosque is taken

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of leading prayers at a mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the setter (I'M) is A M-leader, and an imam is a leader in a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the man who leads prayers in a mosque, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Demolish testament in dreadful tirade, ultimately

indicators.note: the testament abbreviation sits inside the word for dreadful

parts.note: dreadful means dismal
NT is the abbreviation for New Testament

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word tirade

explanation.surface: Someone tears apart a will in the course of an angry rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dismantle a structure is to take it apart or demolish it.

clue.text: Say 'Florida', possibly?

definitions.meaning: to say something is to declare or assert it
Florida is one of the fifty in the USA, an example of a political region

explanation.surface: Whether to say 'Florida' or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to declare; noun sense: a constituent unit of the USA such as Florida.

clue.text: Reading article the wrong way

indicators.note: arranged the wrong way means the letters of article are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone reads a newspaper article but misunderstands it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the act of reading the article, but it is the noun: a public performance of reading or music.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance such as a poetry reading given to an audience.

clue.text: Clear answers billions initially work out

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word billions

parts.note: to work out a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: Instructions for an exam: get the answers clear, starting with the billions, and work it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to clear someone of blame is to absolve them.

clue.text: Novel ending mercifully, maybe another starts?

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the four words ending, mercifully, maybe, another are taken

explanation.surface: A reader hopes a long novel finishes soon and that a sequel begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel ending' looks like the definition with an ending, but Novel stands alone; the starts are of the four following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jane Austen's Emma is a famous English novel of 1815.

clue.text: Fruit eaten up by rhino, lemons

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
eaten by means the letters are swallowed inside the words rhino, lemons

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros munches lemons as if they were fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a melon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family.

clue.text: Sweet wine gets more trembling?

parts.note: a sweet is dessert, called afters in British slang
hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A dessert wine makes someone tremble even more.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the pudding course is often called afters, and Rhine white wine is traditionally called hock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: an aftershock is a further tremor following the main earthquake, so more trembling.

clue.text: Prisons around extravagant country residences

indicators.note: the word for prisons goes around the abbreviation for extravagant

parts.note: cages are prisons for animals
OTT is the abbreviation for over the top, extravagant

explanation.surface: Former jails turned into lavish homes in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cottages are small houses, typically in rural villages and the countryside.

clue.text: Confused, like a sailor?

definitions.meaning: lost, bewildered, not knowing what to do
a sailor on a voyage is out on the ocean

explanation.surface: A sailor described as baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being at sea means bewildered; literally it describes a sailor out on the ocean.

clue.text: Lost cause, rotten stew

indicators.note: rotten suggests decay and breaking down, so the letters of lost cause are reworked

explanation.surface: A failed attempt at a stew that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: cassoulet is a French slow-cooked stew of beans, sausage and duck.

clue.text: A payment secured by friend of father and mother?

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the word for friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
rent is a regular payment for a property

explanation.surface: A payment held in trust by a family friend on behalf of a child's parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective relation: parental means relating to a parent, both father and mother.

clue.text: Half a score otherwise for singer

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half of it is ten
or introduces an alternative, meaning otherwise

explanation.surface: A singer scoring only half marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical next to 'singer' but here means twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

clue.text: Rubbish fish's served with batter

parts.note: the cod is a fish, with the possessive s
to batter is to hit hard, to wallop

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a fish-and-chip shop's battered cod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' suggests the frying coating but means to hit hard. Codswallop is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: codswallop is British slang for nonsense, rubbish talk.

clue.text: Capitol out of sight

indicators.note: out signals the letters of Capitol are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: The US Capitol building cannot be seen from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective relation: optical means relating to vision or the eyes.

clue.text: Comedic, common error that's come up in church

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: common, as in vulgar, means low

indicators.note: come up in a down clue means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: A vulgar faux pas made during a church service is found funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clownish means like a clown, comic or foolish, hence comedic.

clue.text: Shingle shifted from some UK shores?

indicators.note: shifted means the letters of shingle are moved around

explanation.surface: Pebbles on a British beach moved by the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: Shingle is the pebbly material of many British beaches; the definition is a sly hint at coming from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective relation: English describes people or things from England, one part of the UK.

clue.text: One racing out of control, showing lack of awareness

indicators.note: out of control means the letters of one racing go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver racing recklessly shows they are oblivious to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ignorance is a lack of knowledge or awareness.

clue.text: Drug used in growing muscle, or in weight-loss programmes, contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily means the whole is read the opposite way, backwards
in places the word or inside the word for weight-loss programmes

parts.note: diets are weight-loss programmes

explanation.surface: A drug used either for bodybuilding or for slimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrarily' turns round the whole assembly, DIORETS, so it reads in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: anabolic steroids are drugs used by bodybuilders to build muscle.

clue.text: Loss of hope in the French couple

parts.note: des is a French form meaning of the or some
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French couple losing hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: despair is the complete loss or absence of hope.

clue.text: Poisoner tainted sarnie with dash of cyanide

indicators.note: tainted means spoiled, so the letters of sarnie are spoiled into a new order
a dash of means just a small amount, the opening letter of cyanide

explanation.surface: A murderer laces a sandwich with a touch of cyanide.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: arsenic is a notorious poison, a substance that poisons.

clue.text: Illness — I left people in bath scratching both ends!

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside what remains of the word bath
scratching both ends means the first and last letters of the word bath are removed

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Someone with a skin complaint scratches all over in the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ailment is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: How much interest regarding pinafore!

parts.note: APR, annual percentage rate, states how much interest is charged on a loan
on means regarding or about

explanation.surface: Someone surprised at the price of a pinafore.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pinafore is a garment tied over clothes, like an apron.

clue.text: Tory privilege

definitions.meaning: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A jibe that Conservatives stand for privilege.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: right-wing in politics, as Tories are, and an entitlement or prerogative.

clue.text: One thus set on fire, a refinery gutted

parts.note: so means thus
lit is set on fire

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of the word refinery are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Report of an oil refinery set ablaze and burnt out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a number or pronoun; it is the definition, meaning single.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: solitary means single or alone, just one.

clue.text: Grabbing first of toys, old king and I play together

indicators.note: grabbing means the king's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian king

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word toys

explanation.surface: A boy king grabs toys and joins in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests children's games but is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: tutti is an instruction for all performers to play together.

clue.text: God has Egyptian seaport to set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is raised, read backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: Suez is a port city in Egypt

explanation.surface: A deity founding an Egyptian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Zeus is the chief god of the ancient Greek pantheon.

clue.text: Member is slow to establish laws

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
late means behind time, slow

explanation.surface: A member of parliament is slow to pass legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, but here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to legislate is to make or enact laws.

clue.text: Dash can get shortened

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: shortened means the word get loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to be able to get away quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dash of colour is a slight trace or tinge.

clue.text: Essence: it is in pub

indicators.note: in puts the word it inside the pub abbreviation

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the heart of life is the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the pith of an argument is its core or essential part.

clue.text: Beauty — small-minded nature about right

indicators.note: about means the word for small-minded nature goes around the right abbreviation

parts.note: pettiness is a small-minded nature

explanation.surface: A judgement on a pageant contestant: lovely, but petty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: prettiness is attractiveness, a mild form of beauty.
